cards.text: This is a Maskil of David, king of Israel, a song written for the choirmaster. It opens on a man talking to himself. Not out loud, friend, but down in his heart.

cards.question: In David's song, what does the fool say in his heart?

answers.text: That God is on his side

cards.text: David calls that man a fool. Then he widens out to a whole crowd: "They are corrupt; their ways are vile."

cards.question: True or false: David says some of these corrupt people still do good.

cards.text: Now the song looks up, because God is looking down on the sons of men. Picture me crouched at the oven window, squinting at a batch, whispering, "Come on. SOMEBODY in there rise."

cards.question: God looks down from ___ upon the sons of men.
When God looks down on the sons of men, what is He looking for?

answers.text: Anyone who understands and seeks Him
Anyone strong enough to rule them
Anyone who has built Him an altar

cards.question: So what does God find when He looks down on the sons of men?

cards.text: All have turned away and together become corrupt, and no one does good, not even one. Friend, that's not one burnt cookie on the tray. That's the WHOLE TRAY.
Then David asks, "Will the workers of iniquity never learn?" I ask myself the same thing every time I grab a hot tray without a mitt.

cards.question: In the song, how do the workers of iniquity treat "my people"?
True or false: the workers of iniquity refuse to call upon God.

cards.text: Then the song flips: "There they are, overwhelmed with dread, where there was nothing to fear." That's me when my oven ticks as it cools, and I spin around on my base, mustache up, ready to fight an OVEN.

cards.question: In David's song, who scatters the bones of those who besieged you?
True or false: those besiegers are put to shame because God has despised them.

cards.text: David ends with a longing for Israel's salvation. And he pictures the day God restores His captive people.

cards.question: David longs for the salvation of Israel to come from ___.
When God restores His captive people, let Jacob ___, let Israel be ___!

findings.problem: Cards 2, 6, 7, 11, 14 and 17 provide no earlier-card basis for reliably distinguishing the right answer from the alternatives. That makes six of the eleven choices dependent on luck or prior Bible knowledge, so discovery questions dominate instead of remaining a few.

rule.text: A few discovery questions are fine. Some moments can't be reasoned out, like where Jonah's ship is headed. A few of those are okay, as long as most choice cards are informed guesses.

findings.problem: Card 5 does not supply heaven or enough context to infer it rather than Sinai or Carmel. The blank therefore asks for unrevealed wording instead of testing a meaning the baker can reason out.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: Card 16 never mentions Zion or provides a way to distinguish it from Egypt or Babylon. The baker can only guess the unrevealed place name or rely on prior knowledge.
